examples.question_text:
Convert to the requested smaller units.
(a) $3$ minutes $47$ seconds to seconds
(b) $2$ days $11$ hours to hours
(c) $1$ day $6$ hours $13$ minutes to minutes

Convert to whole larger units and the remaining smaller units.
(a) $428$ minutes to hours and minutes
(b) $83$ hours to days and hours
(c) $8429$ seconds to hours, minutes and seconds
examples.solution_text:
(a) $428=7\times60+8$, so $7\text{ h }8\text{ min}$.
(b) $83=3\times24+11$, so $3\text{ days }11\text{ h}$.
(c) $8429=2\times3600+1229$.
$1229=20\times60+29$.
The interval is $2\text{ h }20\text{ min }29\text{ s}$.

examples.question_text: Use a calculator to write $5.28472$ hours as hours, minutes and seconds. Give seconds to 2 decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Enter $5.28472$ and use the DMS key to display hours, minutes and seconds.
The display gives $5$ hours $17$ minutes $4.992$ seconds.
Check the parts: $0.28472\times60=17.0832$ minutes.
$0.0832\times60=4.992$ seconds.
Rounding only the seconds gives $5\text{ h }17\text{ min }4.99\text{ s}$.

examples.question_text: Use a calculator to write $1$ hour $28$ minutes $43$ seconds as decimal hours, to 3 decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
Use the DMS key to enter the hours, minutes and seconds, then display the decimal value.
$1+\dfrac{28}{60}+\dfrac{43}{3600}=1.478611\ldots$ hours.
The interval is approximately $1.479\text{ h}$, to 3 decimal places.

examples.question_text:
Convert the clock times.
(a) $9{:}26\text{ pm}$ to 24-hour time
(b) $12{:}38\text{ am}$ to 24-hour time
(c) $16{:}53$ to 12-hour time
(d) $12{:}07$ to 12-hour time
examples.solution_text:
(a) Add $12$ to the pm hour: $9+12=21$, giving $21{:}26$.
(b) The hour after midnight is $00$, giving $00{:}38$.
(c) $16-12=4$, giving $4{:}53\text{ pm}$.
(d) Keep the noon hour as $12$, giving $12{:}07\text{ pm}$.
